title: Add shortcut keys to the keyboard managerIf you start WeChat or TIM, the shortcut keys will be invalid
author: wisheen
summary: Launching WeChat or TIM disables Keyboard Manager shortcuts until those applications close and PowerToys restarts, indicating a reproducible low-level input-hook compatibility failure.

confidence.rationale: The lifecycle symptom fits hook-chain interference, but no trace confirms whether callbacks stop, events are consumed, or another application state causes the failure.

judgment.rationale: The issue has a concrete lifecycle sequence and a duplicate was closed into this canonical thread. The current-version status is not confirmed by the original author, but the behavior is specific enough for maintainer-side reproduction.
evidence: Shortcuts work after login, fail after WeChat or TIM starts, and recover only after closing those applications and restarting PowerToys.
Issue 37967 was closed by a maintainer as a duplicate of this same WeChat/TIM compatibility bug.
The report says the applications do not merely claim the same configured shortcut.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with current WeChat/TIM and trace low-level keyboard-hook chain health before and after those processes start.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. This is suitable for a red-confidence design candidate only after a maintainer trace confirms hook-chain loss. Reporter-side generic logs are less useful than controlled local instrumentation around hook registration and callbacks.

proposed_fixes.title: Detect and recover Keyboard Manager hook loss caused by input software
proposed_fixes.root_cause: WeChat/TIM likely changes the low-level keyboard-hook chain or input interception state so Keyboard Manager stops receiving callbacks until PowerToys re-registers its hook during restart.
plan: Instrument hook registration, callback cadence, and removal/error paths while launching and closing WeChat/TIM.
If hook loss is confirmed, add bounded health detection and safe re-registration outside the hook callback, with debounce and telemetry.
Add fault-injection tests for hook-registration failure/replacement and verify no duplicate hooks or lost physical input.
verification: Launch current WeChat/TIM and confirm whether Keyboard Manager callback traffic stops while raw input continues.
Verify a bounded recovery restores remaps without restarting PowerToys and without duplicating shortcut actions.

confidence.rationale: The lifecycle symptom fits hook-chain interference, but no trace confirms whether callbacks stop, events are consumed, or another application state causes the failure.

issue_context.summary: Launching WeChat or TIM disables Keyboard Manager shortcuts until those applications close and PowerToys restarts, indicating a reproducible low-level input-hook compatibility failure.
known_information: The original report used PowerToys 0.89.0 running elevated.
The named configured shortcut launches Remote Desktop.
The external link in the comments is not sufficient public technical evidence for a fix.
inferences: WeChat/TIM may install or reorder a low-level keyboard hook that prevents Keyboard Manager's hook from receiving events, and PowerToys restart re-registers it later in the chain.
A watchdog/re-registration strategy could help, but blindly reinstalling hooks risks loops or input disruption.
issue_context.analysis: This is suitable for a red-confidence design candidate only after a maintainer trace confirms hook-chain loss. Reporter-side generic logs are less useful than controlled local instrumentation around hook registration and callbacks.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue, all comments, labels, and the closed duplicate 37967.
Used the close-app plus restart-PowerToys recovery sequence to narrow the likely boundary to global hook lifetime/order.

reproduce.title: Measure Keyboard Manager hook behavior while launching WeChat or TIM
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys release unless the issue names a required preview build
prerequisites: Current WeChat or TIM in a test environment
setup: Verify the remap works before launching the external application.
Enable focused Keyboard Manager hook diagnostics without recording typed content.
steps: Launch and sign in to WeChat or TIM.
Test the remap and record whether Keyboard Manager callbacks continue.
Close the external application and test again without restarting PowerToys.
Restart PowerToys and compare hook registration/callback state.
reproduce.expected_result: External applications should not permanently disable Keyboard Manager; if hook health is lost, recovery should restore it safely without a full PowerToys restart.
